biography: Hahn was a German radiochemist who investigated radioactive nuclides in Berlin and later led the Max Planck Society. His long collaboration with Meitner preceded the chemical identification of barium with Strassmann in neutron-irradiated uranium, decisive evidence underlying the discovery of nuclear fission. He was awarded the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
contributions: Discovered and studied radioactive nuclides with Meitner and other collaborators
Identified barium in irradiated uranium with Strassmann, providing decisive experimental evidence of fission
Developed radiochemical separation and tracer methods
notes: The discovery of nuclear fission involved the chemical experiments of Hahn and Strassmann and the physical explanation by Meitner and Frisch; their distinct contributions should be retained.
